summary: @servicetitan/confirm-navigation preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package's preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/` into a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js], {cwd: D})` against the shipped `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line bundle using string-array rotation (`WV8StW` rotates a large codepoint-array `n7gIxM`) and hex-mangled identifiers (`_0x...`, `MmgoCP`, `etDiOOB`), with no recoverable plaintext strings, URLs, or function names. The package's advertised purpose is a React navigation-confirmation dialog, which has no legitimate need for an alternate JavaScript runtime or an opaque bundle executed at install time. The runtime swap (executing the payload under a freshly downloaded Bun binary rather than the Node process performing the install) is an analysis-evasion pattern, and the obfuscation blocks inspection of what runs on the installer's host. Installing this package causes arbitrary attacker-authored code to execute on the installer's machine on every `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
